🧠 Crypto News Brief: Markets kick off September with resilience as Bitcoin holds key support near $78,500. Institutional inflows, real-world asset tokenization, and privacy asset surges continue to anchor broader ecosystem confidence. 👑 BlackRock’s BUIDL Fund Hits $2.8 Billion to Reclaim Tokenized Treasury Crown BlackRock's BUIDL fund has expanded to $2.8 billion in assets under management across eight blockchain networks. 78362.subject: Derive’s Record Month
78362.body:
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/eaa70932-7ce4-467e-b338-a662ed575d6a/0xR_NL_Banner_Heading_Wordmark.jpg?t=1776775276)
Caption: 

———————————————————————————

Hi all, happy Tuesday! BTC held firm despite renewed geopolitical risk and rising oil prices, while Strategy returned as a buyer after a 10-week pause. Today, we also examine Derive’s record in August, including XAUT’s early traction and the improving economics of its options business. 

———————————————————————————

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/42e942ec-f31d-4957-8722-a3ac7b121e1e/0xR_NL_Market_Update.png?t=1767631151) [Market Update]
Caption: 

Crypto held firm through the [renewed geopolitical conflict in the Middle East](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/8/30/us-strikes-irans-lark-island-in-first-attack-in-weeks) over the weekend. WTI rose 2.83% to $85.76 on Monday and the S&P 500 fell 0.3%, yet BTC gained 1.1% during regular US trading hours and remained above $78,000. That resilience stood out against BTC’s underperformance this year. It entered the week down 11.3% YTD, compared with gains of 15.1% for the Nasdaq and 11.6% for the S&P 500, after trailing both by more than 30% earlier in the year. 

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/8f9430bb-f0ea-406d-aa16-2593f44a2877/image.png?t=1788268965)
Caption: 

BTC’s relative strength also coincided with Strategy returning as a buyer after a 10-week pause. [A Monday 8-K disclosed](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1050446/000119312526375463/mstr-20260831.htm) the purchase of 4,603 BTC for $369.7M, or an average of $80,318 per BTC. The acquisition was funded through $602.8M of ATM share sales. However, Strategy’s return did not lift the broader treasury-company complex. PURR (-4.9%), BTBT (-4.2%), UPXI (-2.2%) and STKE (-1.9%) traded lower, while MSTR (0.3%), BMNR (0.6%) and SBET (0.2%) finished roughly flat.

At the end of August, 21 of 29 tracked names still traded below the value of their holdings. MSTR’s NAV multiple improved from 0.65 to 0.84 during the month but remained at an approximately 16% discount despite resuming purchases. If crypto prices continue to push upward, a narrowing of those discounts could become the next catalyst for the group. A move above NAV across more companies could restart the accretive issuance cycle that funded additional crypto purchases and supported the sector’s previous advance. 

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/ba68205f-926b-49b0-bcc0-358c1c102b2a/image.png?t=1788268965)
Caption:
